messages.content: i drew one small circle in the middle of a large page. my friend says i should draw more because most of it is empty.
empty space can be part of a picture. you can choose whether you want more on the page. there is no rule that every part must be full.
i want to know if i must draw more.
no. you can choose to keep one small circle if that is the picture you want.
i want the circle to look alone. can the empty space help with that?
yes. space around one small thing can help give that idea. you can keep it empty because it is part of what you want people to see.
write a short explanation i could give my friend.
i left the space empty because i want the circle to look alone on the page.
what if i later want another circle next to it?
you can change the picture and its idea. first it can be about being alone, and later it can be about two things together.
say it simply.
you can draw another circle if your idea changes. the picture does not have to keep its first plan.
give a short answer.
you can change the picture when your idea changes.
can you use asks, asked, and asking in one short story?

a child asks her father what he is making for dinner. he says soup. she is asking because she wants to help. yesterday, she asked the same question and helped with bread. today, he gives her a different small task.
what part is about yesterday?
she asked the same question and helped with bread. asked is used for that past question.
what does is asking add?
it puts us with the question while it is happening in that part of the story. asks can tell what happens, while asked puts it in the past.
can you make it all about yesterday?
a child asked her father what he was making for dinner. he said soup. she was asking because she wanted to help. he gave her a small task, and they worked together.
does a person always ask because they need help?
no. in this story she asks because she wants to help someone else. a question can have different reasons.
ask my last question simply.
does someone always ask because they need help?
write one more reason a person might ask.
a person might ask because they want to learn something new.
can a person be already here but not ready yet?
yes. being here is about place. being ready is about whether they can begin what they came to do. they may be here but still need to put their things away.
say it simply.
yes. they can be here and still need time before starting.
write a short conversation at the library.
are you here yet? yes, i am already here, but i am not ready to read yet. what do you need to do? i need to return my old book first. then i can join you.
does not ready mean they will never read with the other person?
no. yet leaves room for being ready later. the person gives a task to finish before they can join the reading.
answer simply.
no. they plan to return the old book first, then read with the other person.
now write a reply after they return it.
i have returned the old book. i am ready to read with you now.
what changed between the first answer and the last answer?
the task before reading is now done. the person was already there and is ready now.
say it simply.
they were there before, but are ready now.
i found a cup on my desk and do not know whose it is. i want to ask the group without saying someone did something wrong.
you could say: does anyone know whose cup this is? it is on my desk.
if a person says it is theirs, can i ask them to take it?
yes. you can make a simple request: could you take it when you have a moment, please?
what if they say they only put it there because the table was full?
you can understand the reason and still ask for your desk space back. you do not have to call the reason false to say what you need now.
write a kind reply with that idea.
i understand. could you take it when you can? i need the desk for my work now.
does whose cup mean who drank from it last?
not always. someone can use a cup that is not theirs. the person who used it and the person whose cup it is can be different people.
answer simply.
no. the person who used it and the person whose cup it is can be different people.
write a question asking only who used it.
who was using this cup?
my friend said that is enough when i was giving them rice. did they say they did not like it?
no. enough can mean they have as much as they want. it does not by itself say whether they like the food.
use how much in a simple answer.
it can mean they have as much as they want. it does not say whether they like the food.
what can i say back without asking why they want to stop?
you can say: okay. tell me if you would like more later.
say my last question simply.
what can i say without asking why they want to stop?
if they ask for more later, is that a different answer?
it is a new choice at another moment. they can have enough at first and want more later.
say it simply.
they can have enough at first and want more later.
can you make one short story from that?
a person asks for a little rice and says it is enough. later, they enjoy it and ask for more. the first answer was about what they wanted then.
my aunt and father heard the same song and remembered different things. she remembered school, and he remembered a journey.
the same song can bring different ideas to mind. your aunt thought about school, and your father thought about a journey.
say it simply.
they knew the same song, but thought about different parts of their lives.
write a small story where they each tell the other why.

a song comes on the radio while a family sits at the table. the aunt says she learned it at school. the father says he heard it on a train when he went to another town. they both know the words, but each has a different story about hearing them.
does that mean one person learned the wrong song?
no. people do not need to learn a song in the same place or at the same time to know the same words.
use need in a short answer.
no. people do not need to learn a song in the same place or at the same time to know the same words.
ask me a question about a song from my life without choosing a memory for me.
is there a song that makes you think of a person or place?
i asked if we should meet at the park or library, and my friend said neither is open today. does that choose the park?
no. neither says that both of those choices are not open. it does not choose one of them.
what can i ask next?
you could ask: is there another place that would work for us?
my friend says their house is okay after lunch. i do not know if i am free then.
then say you need to check the time before choosing: your house sounds good, but i need to check whether after lunch works for me.
can i keep the place open too?
yes. you could say: i need to check my time before we choose a place. i will tell you when i know.
what if i later say i can come after lunch?
then you can ask if the house is still a good place, because that part was not chosen by both of you yet.
answer simply.
ask whether the house still works. your friend gave it as an idea, but you had not said yes yet.
write the question itself.
is your house still a good place to meet after lunch?
what can kind mean in be kind and what kind of book?
in be kind, it is about being good to someone. in what kind of book, it asks about the type of book.
use type and good to someone.
in be kind, it is about being good to someone. in what kind of book, it asks about the type of book.
can you give a short conversation with both?
what kind of story do you want? one about people helping each other. so a story with kind people? yes, but they can still have a problem to work through together.
use a problem in the last part.
yes, but they can still have a problem to work through together.
does a kind person never say no?
no. a person can say no with care and still be kind.
say that simply.
no. a kind reply does not always have to be yes.
write a kind no to a request for a visit today.
i cannot visit today, but thank you for asking me.
write a short story where a cup moves from the kitchen to a desk and then to a shelf. make it clear who moves it each time.

a father takes a cup from the kitchen to his desk. he leaves it there while answering the phone. later, his daughter needs space to draw and asks if she can move it. he says yes, so she puts it on the shelf. when he comes back, he looks at the desk and asks where it is. she can show him the shelf and say she moved it after asking.
put the last part in the past.
when he came back, he looked at the desk and asked where it was. she showed him the shelf and said she moved it after asking.
did she move it without telling him?
she asked first, and he said yes. she may still need to tell him the new place, but she did not move it without a request.
write the whole story in the past with no new facts.

a father took a cup from the kitchen to his desk. later, his daughter asked if she could move it so she had room to draw. he said yes, and she put it on the shelf. when he came back, she showed him where it was.
where is the cup now at the end?
on the shelf.
i wrote please bring two cups, but i only need one. help me send a short message changing that.
i only need one cup, not two. sorry for the change.
say my request simply.
help me send a short message saying i need one cup instead of two.
can you make it without sorry?
i only need one cup instead of two. thank you.
why is instead of useful here?
it says the new request is one cup. it does not ask for one more cup as well as the two.
explain simply.
one is the whole number you need now, not another cup to add to two.
what if the person already brought two?
then your new message cannot change what they already did. you can thank them and explain that you only need to use one now.
write that reply.
thank you for bringing both. i only need to use one after all.
write a story about a girl who asks a question that makes a family look at an old photo together.

a girl finds an old photo of a garden and asks who is standing near the tree. her mother thinks it is an aunt. her father says it might be a cousin. they bring the picture to the grandmother, who can remember the day. she talks about a visit when the whole family came for lunch. the girl likes hearing the story, but asks them to write the name under the picture so they can remember later.
make the middle part simple.
they bring the picture to the grandmother, who can remember the day. she talks about a visit when the whole family came for lunch.
did the story say the name of the person by the tree?
no. it says that the girl asked, but the story has not given the answer about that person yet.
answer simply.
no. the story has not given the name of the person by the tree.
use name in a short answer.
no name was given for that person yet.
finish with the grandmother saying it is her sister, without choosing a name.
the grandmother says: that is my sister. the family writes that detail under the picture.
picoboi, if i ask could i put the book on the shelf, does that tell you i already put it there?
no. it asks about a possible choice. it does not say the choice has happened.
now i say i put it on the shelf. what do you know?
you told me the book is on the shelf, from that change.
what if i say i might move it to the desk later?
then the desk is a possible later place. the shelf is still the last place you said it was put. might does not make the later move a fact.
can you ask a follow up without saying the move already happened?
would you like to move it to the desk, or are you still thinking about it?
i am still thinking. do not choose for me.
okay. the choice is still open. i will not say that you moved it or that you chose a place you have not chosen.
now make a short note for my story with the choice still open.
the book is on the shelf. she may move it to the desk later, but she has not chosen yet.
say my request simply.
write a short note saying the book is on the shelf and the later move is not chosen yet.
